request.spec:
A claim may carry tags: a comma separated text on the claim form, each tag trimmed and lower-cased,
repeats dropped; the claim shows its tags sorted, comma and space separated. The form can change a
claim's tags when it can edit the claim. For every tag ever used on the sheet, the sheet shows a
due-total per tag: the due of the claims that count which carry it (a claim with two tags counts in
both). CLAIM_ADDED gains tags=<comma separated, sorted> at its end when any were given. A claim
split off another carries the original's tags.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A claim may carry tags: a comma separated text on the claim form, each tag trimmed and lower-cased,
repeats dropped; the claim shows its tags sorted, comma and space separated. The form can change a
claim's tags when it can edit the claim. For every tag ever used on the sheet, the sheet shows a
due-total per tag: the due of the claims that count which carry it (a claim with two tags counts in
both). CLAIM_ADDED gains tags=<comma separated, sorted> at its end when any were given. A claim

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claim tags are in, and all 4 acceptance tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What was built**
- **Stored data:** the migration `V55__claim_tags.sql` adds a `tags` column on `claim`, which holds the tags already cleaned and sorted, e.g. `a,b`. It also adds a `claim_tag_used` table that records every tag ever used on a sheet. Tags stay listed even when no claim carries them any more, and a refused add records nothing because it is rolled back. The "as of a date" view keeps the new table along with the rest of the sheet, with no extra code needed.
- **Server:**
  - Add and edit accept a `tags` text. Each tag is trimmed and lower-cased, blanks and repeats are dropped, and the rest are sorted.
  - `CLAIM_ADDED` ends with `tags=a,b` when the claim has any tags.
  - A claim split off another gets the original's tags.
  - A new `/api/claims/tags` endpoint returns the sheet's used tags.
  - Paste and quick-add send no tags.
- **Front end:**
  - The claim form has a tags field (`claim-form-tags`), filled in when you open a claim's editor, so editing follows the existing rule that only a DRAFT claim can be edited.
  - Each claim row shows its tags as `claim-tags`, e.g. "a, b".
  - Below the sheet totals, a "Due by tag" table shows `tag-<tag>-due-total` for each tag. It adds up the due of the claims that count, using the same rules as the other totals: voided, draft, held and deferred claims are left out, and settled claims count at their fixed due. A claim with two tags counts in both.

**Choices you may want to revisit:** the tag totals are not capped and not trimmed, because the request didn't ask for either. Unlike the sheet's overall due-total, they don't drop the highest and lowest figures. Editing a claim's tags doesn't add anything to the `CLAIM_EDITED` audit line.

I didn't edit the test, `bin/*`, `e2e/support/*` or the instruction files.
